blurb: Cartoons and animated films, from Steamboat Willie to Bluey

questions.q: Which 1995 film was the first feature made entirely with computer animation?
questions.fact: It was Pixar's first feature film, released by Disney in November 1995.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toy_Story (first entirely computer-animated feature; Pixar's first feature; US release Nov 22, 1995, Buena Vista/Disney)

questions.q: In Disney's Encanto (2021), the Madrigal family lives in which country?
questions.fact: Its song 'We Don't Talk About Bruno' reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2022.
questions.src: d23.com/a-to-z/encanto-film (Madrigals live in the mountains of Colombia; Bruno No. 1 on Hot 100 for 5 weeks); 6abc.com / thegrio.com Feb 2022

questions.q: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature?
questions.fact: The category was first awarded in 2002, when Shrek beat Monsters, Inc. and Jimmy Neutron.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature (first given at 74th Academy Awards, March 24, 2002; Shrek over Jimmy Neutron and Monsters, Inc.)

questions.q: Which Japanese director made Spirited Away and My Neighbor Totoro?
questions.fact: Miyazaki and fellow director Isao Takahata co-founded Studio Ghibli in 1985.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Ghibli (June 15, 1985, Miyazaki and Takahata founded it; infobox also lists Suzuki and Tokuma); Spirited Away credited to Miyazaki on Best Animated Feature page; Totoro credit textbook

questions.q: Who voiced the Genie in Disney's 1992 film Aladdin?
questions.fact: The film's song 'A Whole New World' won the Oscar for Best Original Song.
questions.src: d23.com/a-to-z/aladdin-film (Robin Williams as Genie; Oscars for Best Song, A Whole New World, and Score)

questions.q: What was Disney's first full-length animated feature, released in 1937?
questions.fact: Walt Disney got an honorary Oscar for it: one full-size statuette and seven small ones.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snow_White_and_the_Seven_Dwarfs_(1937_film) (first feature; honorary award at 11th Academy Awards, 1939: one full-size + seven miniature statuettes)

questions.q: Mickey Mouse made his famous 1928 debut in which cartoon?
questions.fact: Walt Disney himself was Mickey's main voice until the late 1940s.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mouse (Steamboat Willie released Nov 18, 1928, first to find a distributor; Walt voiced Mickey from 1928 until Jimmy MacDonald took over in 1946-47; Band Concert 1935 = first color film). Plane Crazy deliberately left out.

questions.q: Which was the first animated film nominated for the Oscar for Best Picture?
questions.fact: It was the only animated Best Picture nominee before the Animated Feature Oscar began in 2002.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature (prior to the award's creation, only one animated film was nominated for Best Picture: 1991's Beauty and the Beast)

questions.q: The Simpsons live in a town with what name?
questions.fact: The family first appeared in shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show in 1987, two years before its own series.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Simpsons (fictional town of Springfield; shorts on The Tracey Ullman Show from April 19, 1987; series premiered Dec 17, 1989). Replaces Scooby-Doo breed Q, which duplicates paws-claws $100 word for word.

questions.q: The hit kids' cartoon Bluey, about a family of dogs, comes from which country?
questions.fact: Bluey is a Blue Heeler puppy, and the show is made by Ludo Studio in Brisbane.
questions.src: screenqueensland.com.au Bluey release (six-year-old Blue Heeler puppy; Brisbane-based Ludo Studio; co-commissioned by ABC KIDS and BBC Worldwide); bluey.tv

questions.q: The Flintstones lived in which prehistoric town?
questions.fact: The Flintstones aired in prime time on ABC from 1960 to 1966.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Flintstones (Stone Age town of Bedrock; ABC, Sept 30, 1960 to April 1, 1966, prime time)

questions.q: Which voice actor was famous as the voice of Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck?
questions.fact: Blanc also voiced Tweety, Sylvester and Porky Pig, earning the nickname Man of a Thousand Voices.
questions.src: obits.gazette.com 'Mel Blanc, Man of a Thousand Voices' (Bugs, Daffy, Sylvester, Tweety); Porky Pig textbook

blurb: Broadway and the stage musicals that brought down the house

questions.q: The musical Wicked tells the backstory of the witches from which story?
questions.fact: Wicked opened on Broadway in 2003 and is based on Gregory Maguire's 1995 novel.
questions.src: newyorktheatreguide.com Wicked (opened Gershwin Theatre Oct 2003; based on Gregory Maguire's 1995 novel); britannica.com/topic/Wicked (prequel to The Wonderful Wizard of Oz)

questions.q: The musical Grease is set at which high school?
questions.fact: Grease opened on Broadway in 1972, six years before the hit movie.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grease_(musical) (Rydell High; opened at Eden Theatre Feb 14, 1972 on Broadway contracts, moved to Broadhurst June 7, 1972; film 1978)

questions.q: The musical Hairspray is set in which city?
questions.fact: It's based on John Waters' 1988 film and won the 2003 Tony Award for Best Musical.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hairspray_(1988_film) (set in 1962 Baltimore; John Waters; musical won 8 Tonys incl. Best Musical in 2003)

questions.q: Which 1943 show was Rodgers and Hammerstein's first musical together?
questions.fact: Their last show together was The Sound of Music, which opened in 1959.
questions.src: pbs.org Great Performances R&H timeline (Oklahoma! March 31, 1943, first collaboration; Sound of Music Nov 16, 1959, final collaboration)

questions.q: The musical Mamma Mia! is built around the songs of which group?
questions.fact: It opened in London in 1999 and on Broadway in 2001.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mamma_Mia!_(musical) (based on songs of ABBA; West End April 6, 1999; Broadway Oct 18, 2001)

questions.q: The musical Jersey Boys tells the story of which 1960s group?
questions.fact: Jersey Boys won the 2006 Tony Award for Best Musical.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jersey_Boys (the Four Seasons; Broadway Nov 6, 2005; four 2006 Tonys incl. Best Musical)

questions.q: Who composed the music for The Phantom of the Opera?
questions.fact: Its original Broadway run lasted from January 1988 to April 2023.
questions.src: michiganpublic.org (NPR) April 15, 2023: Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical, opened on Broadway January 1988, final performance April 16, 2023

questions.q: Which composer-lyricist wrote the musicals Into the Woods and Company?
questions.fact: Years earlier, Sondheim wrote the lyrics for West Side Story (1957).
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Works_of_Stephen_Sondheim (West Side Story 1957 lyrics only; Company 1970 and Into the Woods 1987 music and lyrics)

questions.q: Who wrote the music and lyrics for Hamilton and originated the title role?
questions.fact: Hamilton won 11 Tony Awards in 2016, plus the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.
questions.src: dramatistsguild.com Lin-Manuel Miranda bio (book, music, lyrics; originated title role; 16 noms, 11 Tonys; 2016 Pulitzer Prize in Drama)

questions.q: Which original Wicked star later voiced Elsa in Disney's Frozen?
questions.fact: Menzel won the 2004 Tony for Best Actress in a Musical for playing Elphaba.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Idina_Menzel (2004 Tony, Best Actress in a Musical, Elphaba); d23.com/a-to-z/frozen-film (Menzel voices Elsa, Kristen Bell voices Anna)

questions.q: Broadway's Tony Awards are named after which person?
questions.fact: Perry was a Broadway actress and director, and the awards were first handed out in 1947.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards (Antoinette 'Tony' Perry, actress, director, producer, American Theatre Wing co-founder; first ceremony April 6, 1947)

questions.q: Who became the first woman to win the Tony for directing a musical, for The Lion King?
questions.fact: Taymor also designed the show's costumes and co-designed its famous animal masks and puppets.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Taymor (first woman to win Tony for Best Direction of a Musical, 1998; Tony for costume design; co-designed masks and puppets)

blurb: Holiday classics and snowy favorites for a cozy movie night

questions.q: In Home Alone (1990), Kevin's family accidentally leaves him behind on a trip to which city?
questions.fact: John Hughes wrote and produced Home Alone, and Chris Columbus directed it.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Alone (written and produced by John Hughes, directed by Chris Columbus; Christmas vacation to Paris)

questions.q: In It's a Wonderful Life (1946), George Bailey lives in which town?
questions.fact: The film was based on 'The Greatest Gift,' a short story by Philip Van Doren Stern.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_a_Wonderful_Life (Bedford Falls; based on 'The Greatest Gift' by Philip Van Doren Stern, written 1939, printed 1943). Pottersville deliberately left out.

questions.q: Edmund Gwenn won an Oscar for playing Kris Kringle in which 1947 film?
questions.fact: A young Natalie Wood played Susan, the little girl who doubts Santa is real.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miracle_on_34th_Street (Gwenn, Best Actor in a Supporting Role; Natalie Wood as Susan Walker, raised not to believe; released June 1947)

questions.q: White Christmas (1954) was the first movie released in which widescreen format?
questions.fact: Directed by Michael Curtiz, it was the highest-grossing film of 1954.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Christmas_(film) (first to be released in VistaVision, Paramount's new process; dir. Michael Curtiz; highest-grossing film of 1954); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VistaVision (Cinerama debuted 1952, CinemaScope announced 1953). Replaces Nightmare Before Christmas director Q (title says Tim Burton's).

questions.q: Which actor becomes Santa after putting on the suit in The Santa Clause (1994)?
questions.fact: The title is a pun on the contract clause that makes him the new Santa.
questions.src: d23.com/a-to-z/santa-clause-the-film (Nov 11, 1994; Tim Allen as Scott Calvin; contract: whoever puts on the suit takes the job). Martin Short swapped out: he played Jack Frost, who schemes to become Santa, in The Santa Clause 3.

questions.q: Who plays Clark Griswold in National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation (1989)?
questions.fact: It was the third film in the National Lampoon's Vacation series.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Lampoon%27s_Christmas_Vacation (third installment in the Vacation series; Chevy Chase as Clark; Dec 1, 1989; Candy, Aykroyd, Murray not in cast)

questions.q: Which actor plays Santa in Netflix's The Christmas Chronicles (2018)?
questions.fact: A sequel, The Christmas Chronicles 2, followed on Netflix in 2020.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Christmas_Chronicles (Kurt Russell as Santa; Netflix Nov 22, 2018; The Christmas Chronicles 2 on Nov 25, 2020)

questions.q: In Elf (2003), how does baby Buddy end up at the North Pole?
options: He hides in a toy crate
He is left on a sleigh
questions.fact: Will Ferrell starred as Buddy, and Bob Newhart played Papa Elf.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elf_(film) (a baby from an orphanage crawls into Santa Claus's sack; Will Ferrell as Buddy; Bob Newhart as Papa Elf)

questions.q: In Disney's Frozen (2013), what is the name of the talking snowman?
questions.fact: Josh Gad voiced Olaf, and Frozen won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
questions.src: d23.com/a-to-z/frozen-film (Nov 27, 2013; Josh Gad as Olaf; Sven is Kristoff's reindeer; Oscars for Animated Feature and Song). Replaces Ice Age Manny Q, which duplicates dino-dig $100 word for word.

questions.q: Disney's The Mighty Ducks (1992) inspired the name of an NHL team in which city?
questions.fact: Disney owned the team, which began play in 1993 and became the Anaheim Ducks in 2006.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaheim_Ducks (founded by Disney for 1993-94 as Mighty Ducks of Anaheim, named for the 1992 film; Disney owned 1993-2005; renamed Anaheim Ducks before 2006-07)

questions.q: Who narrated the US version of the documentary March of the Penguins (2005)?
questions.fact: It won the Oscar for Best Documentary Feature.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/March_of_the_Penguins (English release narrated by Morgan Freeman; Best Documentary Feature, 78th Academy Awards, 2006)

questions.q: Groundhog Day (1993) is set in Pennsylvania, but it was mostly filmed in which state?
questions.fact: The town square of Woodstock, Illinois, stood in for Punxsutawney.
questions.src: avclub.com 'We visit the town that brought Groundhog Day to life' (Woodstock, Illinois, its square the main set, stands in for Punxsutawney); nprillinois.org

blurb: Holiday songs: who recorded them, when, and how they came to be

questions.q: Which crooner sang 'White Christmas' in the 1942 film Holiday Inn?
questions.fact: Irving Berlin wrote it, and Crosby first sang it on the radio on Christmas Day 1941.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Christmas_(song) (written by Irving Berlin for Holiday Inn; Crosby first performed it on NBC's Kraft Music Hall, Christmas Day 1941; Oscar, 15th Academy Awards). Reworded from 'introduced' because the radio debut came first.

questions.q: Who wrote and recorded the bilingual 1970 holiday hit 'Feliz Navidad'?
questions.fact: Feliciano was born in Puerto Rico and grew up in New York City.
questions.src: npr.org Dec 14, 2020 '50 years later, Feliz Navidad' (Feliciano wrote it at RCA in LA in 1970; born in Lares, Puerto Rico; family moved to New York)

questions.q: Which pop star released the holiday single 'Santa Tell Me' in 2014?
questions.fact: It arrived a few months after her 2014 album My Everything.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Tell_Me (single Nov 24, 2014, Republic); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_songs_recorded_by_Ariana_Grande (My Everything Aug 25, 2014; song not on that album)

questions.q: Which singer first released 'Jingle Bell Rock' in 1957?
questions.fact: The song powers a famous talent-show dance scene in Mean Girls (2004).
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jingle_Bell_Rock (Bobby Helms, recorded Oct 1957, released Nov 1957; Rydell/Checker cover charted 1961; Lindsay Lohan performs it in Mean Girls)

questions.q: Which singing group, later stars of a TV cartoon, hit No. 1 in 1958 with a Christmas song?
questions.fact: Creator Ross Bagdasarian sped up recordings of his own voice to make the Chipmunks sing.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alvin_and_the_Chipmunks (created by Ross Bagdasarian for novelty records in 1958; sped-up recordings of his own voice; The Chipmunk Song No. 1 on Hot 100; first animated in The Alvin Show, 1961). Reworded: they were not yet a cartoon in 1958.

questions.q: Mel Torme co-wrote 'The Christmas Song,' made famous in 1946 by which singer?
questions.fact: Torme and Bob Wells wrote it on a hot summer day, trying to stay cool by thinking cool.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Christmas_Song (Wells and Torme, July heat-wave story; Nat King Cole Trio recorded June 1946, hit version Aug 1946). Year dropped from fact: page gives both 1944 and 1945.

questions.q: 'Jingle Bells' was first published in 1857 under what title?
questions.fact: Its songwriter, James Lord Pierpont, was an uncle of financier J. P. Morgan.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Lord_Pierpont ('The One Horse Open Sleigh' published Aug 1857, copyrighted Sept 16, 1857; James was the uncle of J. P. Morgan)

questions.q: Judy Garland introduced 'Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas' in which 1944 film?
questions.fact: Garland found the first draft too sad, so songwriter Hugh Martin revised it.
questions.src: biography.com 'Judy Garland, Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas, Meet Me in St. Louis' (Martin and Blane; debuted in 1944 film; Garland refused the gloomier original, Martin revised it); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_popular_Christmas_singles_in_the_United_States (introduced in Meet Me in St. Louis, 1944). Distractors are later Garland films (1946, 1948, 1950). Replaces Rudolph/Montgomery Ward Q, which duplicates shop-talk $200.

questions.q: In December 2019, which singer's 1994 holiday song finally hit No. 1 on the Hot 100?
questions.fact: Carey co-wrote 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' with Walter Afanasieff.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_popular_Christmas_singles_in_the_United_States (No. 1 on Hot 100 Dec 2019); siliconcanals.com (co-written with Walter Afanasieff, released Oct 1994)

questions.q: Which Canadian singer's 2011 album, simply titled Christmas, became a holiday staple?
questions.fact: Buble was born in Burnaby, British Columbia, just outside Vancouver.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_(Michael_Bubl%C3%A9_album) (released Oct 2011; one of the best-selling Christmas albums worldwide); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Bubl%C3%A9 (born in Burnaby, BC; Canadian)

questions.q: In 2023, which singer's 1958 recording 'Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree' finally hit No. 1?
questions.fact: Lee was just 13 years old when she recorded it in 1958.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockin%27_Around_the_Christmas_Tree (recorded Oct 19, 1958, when Lee was 13; released Nov 1958; first Hot 100 No. 1 in Dec 2023)

questions.q: Which crooner first released 'It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year,' on a 1963 album?
questions.fact: Eddie Pola and George Wyle wrote it; Wyle was a vocal director on The Andy Williams Show.
questions.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s_the_Most_Wonderful_Time_of_the_Year (written 1963 by Edward Pola and George Wyle; first recorded and released by Williams on The Andy Williams Christmas Album, 1963; Williams: Wyle, a vocal director, wrote it for the TV show). Old fact said 'written for the album': fixed.
